neighbours.label: the connective ' so' joining a cause to its consequence or purpose mid-sentence (also Japanese ので / Korean 므로)
fire: The bridge was closed for repairs so we drove the long way around the lake.
She had already read the report twice, so the meeting held no surprises for her.
The bakery ran out of flour early so the owners shut the doors at noon.
We packed extra blankets so that the children would stay warm overnight.
His train was delayed by an hour, so he missed the opening speech entirely.
The paint was still wet so nobody was allowed to touch the railing.
They booked the hall months ahead so the wedding could go ahead in June.
The river had flooded the field, so the farmers moved the sheep uphill.
quiet: The bridge was closed for repairs and we drove the long way around the lake.
She had already read the report twice, but the meeting still surprised her.
The bakery ran out of flour early because the delivery truck broke down.
We packed extra blankets while the children watched cartoons in the den.
His train was delayed by an hour, and he arrived during the closing speech.
The paint was still wet when the inspector came to look at the railing.
They booked the hall months ahead and sent the invitations in March.
The river had flooded the field after three days of steady autumn rain.

notes: card: ' so' x17 of top 32 plus ので/므로; the - pole is the comma/'Therefore' before a main clause. Near misses swap 'so' for 'and', 'but', 'because' or 'while'.
